note: Wikidata q-ids only, searched in Dutch and confirmed by description. Centre is the Explorer product's centre for Amsterdam on origin/main, not Wikidata's point for the city (Q727 sits on Dam Square itself, which would flag the Dam as a centroid mistake). Ten of these sixteen places are carried over from the Explorer product; docs/world/research/explorer-pins.json already audited their q-ids and every one graded ok except Vondelpark (the Explorer pin stood at the east gate, 1143 m from the park's own centroid — the item is right, the anchor is 'area') and De Waag (unmatched there; Q2466999 is the weigh house building). Three q-ids suggested for the museums in the brief were wrong items and were not used: Q1969011 is a Polish gmina, Q1200631 a grammatical mood and Q17431 an airport on Réunion; the museums are Q1422000 (NEMO), Q1616123 (Het Scheepvaartmuseum) and Q165366 (Anne Frank House). No entrance is claimed anywhere: no door here has been measured, so every point is the centroid or area it actually is, and where a venue's own page names its door the city file carries a findIt sentence instead.

places.name: Anne Frank House
places.note: The museum item, which is also the house at Prinsengracht 263; the separate building item Q64265287 carries no coordinate. Declared adjacent to the Westerkerk, which stands beside it — they are about 80 m apart, above the floor, but they are real neighbours and the pair is on record.

places.name: Vondelpark
places.note: The pin audit marked the Explorer pin 'wrong' because it stood at the Stadhouderskade gate, 1143 m from the park's centroid. The item is the park; the honest anchor for a 47-hectare park is 'area', and the gate is given in words in the city file's findIt.

places.name: De Waag
places.note: Unmatched in the pin audit. Q2466999 is the 15th-century weigh house building on the Nieuwmarkt, not the Waag Society that occupies its upper floors.

places.name: Het Scheepvaartmuseum
places.note: The museum item carries the coordinate; the building item 's Lands Zeemagazijn (Q33085) is the same arsenal of 1656 and describes the same footprint.
